samples.prompt: <problem>how many different ways can 2 students be seated in a row of 4 desks , so that there is always at least one empty desk between the students ?</problem><operations>a ) 2 , b ) 3 , c ) 4 , d ) 6 , e ) 12</options>
samples.reference: <rationale>"total cases : 12 ( student one has 4 options and student two has three options , 4 x 3 = 12 ) non - favourable cases : 6 ( when two students sit together . students in desk 1 and desk 2 , in desk 2 and desk 3 , in desk 3 and desk 4 ) for each of these cases there are two possibilities because the positions can be interchanged . hence 2 x 3 = 6 . so favourable cases : 12 - 6 = 6 . answer : d"</rationale><correct>d</correct>
samples.prediction: <rationale>"explanation : total number of ways to arrange 2 students = 4 * 3 = 12 now we have to exclude the cases where all 2 students sit together . this means they occupy 2 adjacent seats . let us consider the case when student A sits on left and student B sits on right . then there are only 2 possible arrangements - AB or BA . similarly if student A sits on right and student B sits on left , then there are only 2 possible arrangements - BA or AB . hence total no of ways = 2 + 2 = 4 answer : c"</rationale><correct>c</correct>
